primary_sources.author: Eyal Markman
primary_sources.title: Cycles on abelian 2n-folds of Weil type from secant sheaves on abelian n-folds
used_facts: Theorem 1.5.1 proves algebraicity of Hodge-Weil classes for polarized abelian sixfolds of Weil type with discriminant -1 for every imaginary quadratic K.
The discriminant is det(H) modulo the norm subgroup Q^*/Nm(K^*); (n,K,det H) is a discrete moduli invariant.
The generic Weil-type abelian variety has cyclic Neron-Severi group and a 3-dimensional middle rational Hodge space.

primary_sources.author: Amir Mostaed
primary_sources.title: McMullen's Curve, the Weil Locus, and the Hodge Conjecture for Abelian Sixfolds
used_facts: For g=3, Markman's discriminant -1 result is the general solved locus stated there; outside this locus the Hodge conjecture for Weil classes on sixfolds remains completely open.
The paper isolates absence of K-secant structure and uncontrolled discriminant as independent obstructions to importing the known secant-sheaf theorem.
The discriminant is det(H) modulo Nm(K^*) and is not controlled in the paper's new rigid family.

primary_sources.author: Eyal Markman
primary_sources.title: Secant sheaves on abelian n-folds with real multiplication and Weil classes on abelian 2n-folds with complex multiplication
used_facts: The broader CM-field construction is conditional for algebraicity on semiregularity of the constructed object; the paper states that semiregularity has not been addressed there.
For a Weil-type action, wedge_K^d H^1 is one-dimensional over K and lies in H^{d/2,d/2} under the equal multiplicity condition.
